chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Mūsā ibn ʿUmar ibn Bazīʿ, he said:
I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: "May I tie the waist-wrapper and the kerchief over my shirt during salat (prayer)?" He said: "There is no harm in it."

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act in which this clothing question arises
key_terms.الْإِزَارَ: a waist-wrapper or lower garment tied around the body
key_terms.الْمِنْدِيلَ: a cloth or kerchief worn or tied on the body
key_terms.قَمِيصِي: my shirt, the garment underneath the outer wrapping
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to tie an izar and a cloth over one's shirt during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that wearing and fastening an izar and a cloth over one's shirt during salat (prayer) is permitted. It serves as a legal indication that such dress in prayer is not problematic, despite the chapter heading mentioning dislike.
